plan: [ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Overbidding risks winning at a negative payoff if the second-highest bid exceeds your value; underbidding risks losing when you would have earned positive surplus. With values redrawn independently each round and no learning value from signaling, the optimal long-run profit strategy is truthful bidding each round. Therefore, set bid equal to my value, 26, which is my maximum willingness to pay. ]

[ In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. It ensures you win exactly when the price (second-highest bid) is below your value and maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. With only one round, there’s no benefit to shading or overbidding. My value is $31, so I bid exactly my value. ]

[ In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies and tie-breaking.
